Unit 5: The OOP Paradigm

SL curriculum overview and structured learning plan.

Introduction

How do we build software that mirrors the real world?

This unit marks a paradigm shift from 'doing' (procedural functions) to 'being' (object-oriented programming). You will learn to model software around Objects — distinct entities that combine data (attributes) and behavior (methods) into reusable blueprints called Classes.

You'll start by distinguishing between a Class (the blueprint) and an Object (the house). Then, you'll master UML diagrams to design these structures, learn to control access with Encapsulation, and investigate the difference between data that belongs to an object vs data that belongs to the class (Static).

Classes & Objects

The core philosophy of OOP is modeled on reality:

  • Class: The architectural blueprint or template (e.g., "Car" design).
  • Object: A specific instance built from that blueprint (e.g., "My Red Toyota").
  • Instantiation: The process of creating an object from a class.
UML Diagrams

Before coding, we design using Unified Modeling Language (UML) class diagrams. They have 3 standard sections:

  1. Class Name: (e.g., BankAccount)
  2. Attributes (Fields): Data the object knows (e.g., - balance: double).
  3. Methods (Actions): Things the object does (e.g., + deposit(amount)).

Note symbols: + means Public, - means Private.

Encapsulation

Good objects hide their internal workings. Encapsulation restricts direct access to data ('private variables') and forces external code to use Accessor (Get) and Mutator (Set) methods.

Why Encapsulate?

It protects data integrity. A setAge(-5) method can reject invalid data, whereas direct access p.age = -5 cannot.

Static vs Instance

Not all data belongs to a specific object:

  • Instance Variable: Unique to each object (e.g., myScore).
  • Static Variable: Shared by ALL objects of that class (e.g., totalPlayers).
Key Terminology
TermDefinition
Object-Oriented Programming A paradigm based on the concept of 'objects', which contain data and code: data in the form of fields, and code in the form of procedures.
Class A blueprint or template for creating objects.
Object (Instance) A specific realization of a class, created in memory.
Constructor (__init__) A special method called when an object is instantiated to initialize its attributes.
Attribute A variable that belongs to an object or class.
Method A function that belongs to an object or class.
Encapsulation Bundling data and methods that work on that data within one unit, and restricting access to some of the object's components.
Accessor (Getter) A method used to return the value of a private attribute.
Mutator (Setter) A method used to update the value of a private attribute.
Static A keyword indicating a member belongs to the class itself, not to instances of the class.
